phaser.description: Four all-pass stages swept together by a sine LFO, summed with the dry signal: the notches where they cancel move up and down. rate in Hz (fixed: its phase is the song's), depth in octaves either side of center, feedback 0..1 sharpens the notches (it is the stages' q: all-pass, so no setting can boost or run away), mix 0..1 the swept signal's level. Stereo in, stereo out: spread (degrees, 90 by default; fixed as it is placed) sweeps the right side that far ahead of the left, so a centred sound comes out wide; 0 sweeps both together.

phaser6.name: phaser
phaser6.description: The phaser with six stages, as the classic small pedals have: three notches sweeping instead of two, a deeper, more liquid sweep. It is the phaser (its name) with two more stages: the phaser's options (rate, spread, depth, center, feedback) reach all six through ap*, and mix is the sixth stage's. odawg show SPEC parts/NAME lists them as placed.

flanger.description: A short delay (1 to 5 ms) swept by a slow triangle LFO, fed back into itself and set against the dry signal: a comb of deep notches sliding up and down, the jet sound. rate in Hz (fixed: its phase is the song's), delay in seconds (its center; fixed as the effect is placed), sweep in seconds either side, feedback 0..1 (0.9 at most into the line: it rings, it doesn't run away), spread (degrees, fixed as it is placed: the right side's sweep that far ahead, wide; 0, as written, both together).

tremolo.description: The level rising and falling with a sine LFO: depth 0..1 how far it dips (0.5: to half), rate in Hz (fixed: its phase is the song's, so a tremolo on two parts moves together; a Tone length, "8n", on the beat). Stereo in, stereo out; spread (degrees) dips the sides apart (180: one up as the other is down).

autopan.description: The sound moving between the sides with a sine LFO: width 0..1 how far (1: all the way), rate in Hz (fixed: its phase is the song's).

autowah.description: A band-pass whose center follows how loud the input is: louder opens it up to range octaves above center. A Follower reads the level (attack and release its times); sensitivity in dB is how hard it reads it, q the band's narrowness, dry 0..1 the dry signal under it. For a funk guitar, a clav, a bass.
